text: Provide a safe-mode session: when the shell or compositor exhausts its restart budget, the supervisor starts a minimal recovery shell with settings, log export and os restore.
Define supervision semantics (restart budgets, rebind protocol, readiness reporting) that the V0.5 compositor-restart gate depends on.

lens: Boot, firmware, platform security and identity
text: ADR: early userspace strategy — a native init component that runs before the root store is unlocked, versus reusing a Linux initramfs and systemd for early boot with the native world starting afterwards.
rationale: Disk unlock, verity setup and service supervision all live in early boot, and reusing systemd here risks fossilizing Linux semantics into the native boot path.

lens: Boot, firmware, platform security and identity
text: Build a native init and service supervisor that starts system services as components with declared capabilities, dependency-ordered startup, restart policies and readiness signalling, replacing systemd for the native world.
rationale: §32 requires restartable services but nothing in the baseline owns starting, ordering or supervising them.

text: Settings storage model: settings are typed, schema-versioned objects whose changes are recorded as system history events and restorable via os restore, with a per-application settings API in the SDK.
rationale: Without this, §31 system history cannot restore configuration and every app invents its own config file format.

text: Time service: NTP/NTS client (decision: chrony retained versus native), RTC synchronisation, timezone auto-detection through a location capability, and defined monotonic versus wall-clock semantics for Operation deadlines across suspend.
rationale: TLS, package signing, and deadlines all fail with wrong clocks and suspend/resume clock behaviour must be defined for the async model.

text: Build a supervision and service-management layer (propose new workstream SVC: system services, supervision, restart policy, dependency ordering) that restarts critical user-space services and re-advertises their interfaces.
Study Erlang/BEAM supervision trees and Fuchsia component manager restart policies to design supervision strategies (one-for-one, escalation, backoff).
